stories.headline: Seattle's Backfield Is Wide Open Range and a Rookie Just Rode In Alone
stories.read: The Seahawks put Zach Charbonnet on the shelf to open camp, still mendin' that busted-up knee from February with no date circled on the calendar. Kenneth Walker already lit out for Kansas City, so the whole herd of carries in Seattle now runs behind first-rounder Jadarian Price with nothin' but George Holani and Emanuel Wilson chasin' him. Pardner, a rookie handed the reins with no veteran in the way is the closest thing to free land you'll see all August. Stake that claim before the saloon reads the injury wire and the price doubles.

stories.headline: Atlanta Can't Find a Quarterback in Its Own Camp, and Drake London Pays the Toll
stories.read: Well now, the Falcons opened the tent flaps and neither gunslinger could walk through. Tua Tagovailoa's back flared up and put him on the sideline, Michael Penix Jr. is still stuck in individual and 7-on-7 work while that November ACL heals, and Atlanta got so thin they signed Cooper Rush just to have somebody throw in team drills. That's a whole month of chemistry Drake London and Kyle Pitts ain't gettin', and it's why the saloon's gonna let London slide a round or two come the great land grab. Doc says a hurt back in July is a rumor, not a verdict: let 'em panic, then take the best target on that offense at a discount.

stories.headline: Travis Hunter's Knee Is Healed, But Jacksonville Is Pointin' Him at the Wrong End of the Field
stories.read: Good news out of the doc's tent: Hunter is six months past that torn LCL and fully cleared for camp, ridin' both ways again like nobody else in the territory. Trouble is, Jacksonville has said out loud and repeatedly that he lines up first as their top cornerback, and Liam Coen drafted two tight ends 'cause he wants more of them on the field. That means fewer routes, fewer looks, and a fella whose fantasy price is built on a job he ain't fully got. Hunter's a beautiful horse with a saddle you don't control, so let somebody else in your outfit pay the legend tax while you spend that pick on Brian Thomas Jr.
